observation.initial_state: A close-up shot of a glossy, orange, dome-shaped object resting on a bed of white granular material. The surface of the object is highly reflective with visible specular highlights.
visible_changes: Early (0.0s - 15.0s): The object remains largely static in shape and position, though there are subtle shifts in the reflection patterns on its surface, suggesting slight movement or settling.
Middle (15.0s - 25.0s): A clear deformation begins at the bottom edge of the object. It starts to flatten and spread outwards onto the white granular surface, losing its defined spherical boundary.

Late (25.0s - 33.4s): The spreading process accelerates significantly. The object visibly collapses downwards and expands horizontally, transforming from a dome into a flatter puddle-like shape as it merges with the white grains.
observation.final_state: The orange object has lost its original dome structure, appearing flattened and spread out across the white granular base, resembling a liquid or semi-solid substance that has collapsed.
uncertain_details: The specific material composition of the orange object (e.g., whether it is melting ice cream, collapsing foam, or a viscous fluid) cannot be determined solely from visual evidence.
The cause of the collapse (gravity, heat, structural failure) is not explicitly shown, only the physical result of the deformation.
